Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- The April 2023 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows broad-based tightening in credit supply across C&I, CRE, and most consumer categories (auto, RRE, HELOCs, subprime, other consumer), with wider loan spreads, lower loan-to-value ratios, and higher debt-service coverage ratios. Banks also expect further tightening, including foreign banks—corroborating the FOMC’s warning that tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity, hiring, and inflation.
- Credit demand weakened for key C&I uses (plant/equipment, M&A, inventories, A/R financing), implying softer business investment and slower growth momentum despite robust recent job gains.
- Tightening is driven by a cautious economic outlook, declines in collateral values (notably CRE), higher funding costs, deposit outflows, and liquidity concerns—consistent with post-stress funding pressures.
- Net effect: While the system is “sound and resilient,” SLOOS points to a more pronounced prospective drag on growth and a risk-aware stance. This tilts the tone slightly negative relative to a purely neutral read and supports the Committee’s decision to hold rates and continue balance-sheet reduction while assessing lags.
